## Course Description

Data engineering is the practice of moving data reliably from where it is
produced to where it is used. This course teaches the full lifecycle: ingesting
raw events, modeling and storing them, transforming them into analytics-ready
tables, and operating the whole thing in production without paging someone at
3 a.m.

Students build a working pipeline incrementally across the semester — from a
single ingestion script in Week 2 to a scheduled, tested, monitored ELT system
by the final project. We favor open-source tooling (Python, dbt, Airflow,
DuckDB, Postgres) so nothing here is locked to one vendor.

**Prerequisites:** DATA 2100 (Intro to Python) and one database course, or
instructor permission. Comfort with the command line and basic SQL is assumed.

## Learning Outcomes

By the end of the course, a successful student will be able to:

1. Design a dimensional data model from messy source records and justify the
   grain of each table.
2. Implement idempotent batch ingestion and explain why idempotency matters
   for retries and backfills.
3. Write transformation logic as version-controlled, tested SQL using dbt.
4. Orchestrate multi-step pipelines with explicit dependencies and schedules.
5. Add data-quality tests and basic observability, and triage a failed run from
   logs alone.

## Weekly Schedule

| Wk | Topic | Reading | Lab / Deliverable |
|----|-------|---------|-------------------|
| 1  | What is data engineering; the modern data stack | Reis & Housley Ch. 1–2 | Environment setup |
| 2  | Ingestion patterns: batch vs. streaming | Kleppmann Ch. 11 | Lab 1 — ingest an API feed |
| 3  | Storage & file formats (CSV, Parquet, columnar) | Reis & Housley Ch. 6 | – |
| 4  | Relational modeling & normalization | Kimball Ch. 1–2 | Lab 2 — design a schema |
| 5  | Dimensional modeling: facts & dimensions | Kimball Ch. 3 | – |
| 6  | Transformation with SQL + dbt | dbt docs | Lab 3 — first dbt model |
| 7  | Testing & data quality | Great Expectations guide | Midterm review |
| 8  | **Midterm exam** | — | Midterm |
| 9  | Orchestration concepts & DAGs | Airflow concepts | Lab 4 — schedule a DAG |
| 10 | Incremental models & backfills | dbt incremental docs | – |
| 11 | Observability, logging, alerting | Petrella, *Fundamentals of DQ* | – |
| 12 | Cost & performance: partitioning, pruning | DuckDB docs | Project checkpoint |
| 13 | Streaming primer: Kafka & change data capture | Kleppmann Ch. 11 | – |
| 14 | Data contracts & governance | guest lecture | – |
| 15 | Project work week | — | Office hours only |
| 16 | **Final project presentations** | — | Final project due |

## Grading

Final grades are weighted as follows:

| Component | Weight | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Labs (4 × 8%) | 32% | Hands-on pipeline assignments |
| Midterm exam | 18% | Modeling + ingestion concepts |
| Final project | 35% | End-to-end ELT pipeline + write-up |
| Participation & quizzes | 15% | In-class quizzes, lab peer review |

Letter grades use the standard scale: A ≥ 93, A− ≥ 90, B+ ≥ 87, B ≥ 83,
B− ≥ 80, C+ ≥ 77, C ≥ 73, and so on. There is no curve; if everyone earns an
A, everyone gets an A.

### Final Project

Teams of two build an end-to-end pipeline against a public dataset of their
choosing: ingestion → storage → dbt transformations → at least three
data-quality tests → an orchestrated schedule. Deliverables are a running repo,
a short architecture write-up, and a 10-minute presentation.

## Policies

**Late work.** Labs may be submitted up to 48 hours late for a 15% penalty.
After 48 hours a lab earns no credit unless an extension was arranged in
advance. The final project deadline is firm.

**Collaboration.** Discussing concepts is encouraged. Labs are individual: the
code you submit must be your own. The final project is explicitly a team effort.
Cite any external code you adapt.

**Generative AI.** You may use AI assistants for boilerplate and debugging, but
you must be able to explain every line you submit. Unexplainable code is treated
as uncited external work.

**Accessibility.** Students needing accommodations should contact the
Disability Services office in the first two weeks. Arrangements are confidential
and applied without penalty.

**Communication.** Course announcements go through the LMS. Email responses
within one business day; for code questions, the course discussion forum is
faster and helps your classmates too.
